content:
maya: heads-up — support ticket from AcmeCorp: their EU users seeing p95 ~800ms -> 1.2s and p99 ~2s for generation API since ~06:20Z. They say it started after a config push yesterday. They included traces showing TLS handshake spending 700-900ms. Can SRE/network take a look? :rotating_light:

jordan: pinging infra. any known deploys around that time?

maya: product said there was a small egress-route policy tweak to prefer low-cost hop for us-west->eu traffic at 04:45Z. not sure details.

samira: looking at ingress metrics — spike aligns with 06:18Z. only affects eu-west requests that route to our us-central model pool (we fallback for capacity). eu-only endpoints fine.

liam: I ran a quick traceroute from an EU test node to the us-central VIP. got an extra AS hop and a 250ms jump at hop 5 -> hop 6. suspecting a routing hairpin or detour. paste logs: 

```
traceroute to 34.89.120.11 (34.89.120.11), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.10.1.1  0.6 ms  0.4 ms  0.4 ms
 2  100.64.3.5  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.2 ms
 3  203.0.113.1  8.9 ms  9.0 ms  9.1 ms
 4  198.51.100.5  12.3 ms  12.4 ms  12.6 ms
 5  198.51.101.1  15.6 ms  16.0 ms  15.9 ms
 6  45.76.33.2  270.4 ms  275.1 ms  269.8 ms  <-- big jump
 7  34.89.120.11  277.2 ms  276.9 ms  278.1 ms
```

jordan: that jump at hop6 matches the TLS handshake slowdown numbers (handshake time ~270-300ms * 2 round trips). ops-bot, any recent BGP/route-map changes?

ops-bot: recent-change: route-policy-economy applied to egress-routers at 04:44Z by netops. Change id: rp-2026-0425-0812.

samira: timeline matches. net-bgp-bot, who owns rp-2026-0425-0812?

net-bgp-bot: owner: netops-team. Policy detail: prefer AS-path shorter? prefer cheaper-peers for outbound to cloud-vendor.

liam: can we temporarily revert that policy for traffic destined to our model pool IP blocks? If we force more direct peers it should reduce the AS hop.

maya: agreed — mitigation plan: 1) netops revert route-policy for prefixes 34.89.120.0/24 and 34.89.121.0/24 (our model pool egress), 2) lower DNS TTL on fallback domain so clients pick eu-hosted model sooner, 3) route-shift canary to eu-models for heavy customers. anyone object?

jordan: +1. also let's capture packet traces and TLS logs for a sample client to share with provider. commands I ran: 

```
# from eu test node
dig +short @8.8.8.8 fallback.api.redwood.net
34.89.120.11

curl -w "time_connect:%{time_connect} time_appconnect:%{time_appconnect}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://34.89.120.11/v1/generate
time_connect:0.270 time_appconnect:1.020

sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 34.89.120.11 and port 443 -w /tmp/eu-us-handshake.pcap
```

samira: grabbing a pcap now and collecting TLS log samples. I also see increased DNS resolution variance in our logs — some EU requests resolve to US VIP rather than EU VIP. likely due to the route-policy changing advertised next-hops causing geolocation mapping issues at DNS/CDN layer.

liam: temporary mitigation enacted: netops rolled back rp-2026-0425-0812 for the two prefixes at 06:45Z. initial telemetry shows p95 dropping from 800ms -> 180ms. p99 down to ~350ms.

maya: great — please keep monitoring for further regressions and create a postmortem. next actions: 
- netops: full revert diff and why cheaper-peer policy accepted the detour (ticket with vendor).
- infra: add a health-check that alerts when TLS handshake >200ms for 1m per region.
- devex/product: update fallback config to prefer local-models when possible and reduce DNS TTL to 30s during incidents.

jordan: filing ticket to vendor with pcaps and traceroutes. ticket #NET-5871. adding them to thread.

samira: also noting this impacted customers using Dedicated fallback to US. we should add a routing affinity rule to keep EU-origin traffic in EU unless capacity forcing failover.

maya: thanks all. leaving thread open for 24h. once vendor confirms root-cause we'll draft the postmortem. :memo:
